# Meteor shower calendar

A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece. The Perseid meteor shower peaks in August and often shows dozens of meteors per hour. The ecliptic is tilted about 23.4 degrees to the celestial equator because of the tilt of the Earth. An armillary sphere models the sky with rings for the equator, the ecliptic and the meridian.

## Steps

- Collimation aligns the primary and secondary mirrors so stars focus to a sharp point.
- Light pollution washes out faint galaxies, so a site with a Bortle class of three or lower is worth the drive.
- The four Galilean moons of Jupiter change position every night and are easy to see in binoculars.
- Right ascension is measured in hours along the celestial equator, and declination in degrees north or south of it.
- Saturn rings tilt over a fifteen year cycle, so their appearance slowly changes from year to year.
